title: How Not to Die: Discover the Foods Scientifically Proven to Prevent and Reverse Disease
author: Michael Greger, M.D., with Gene Stone
target_audience: Adults interested in improving overall health and longevity
People with chronic conditions (heart disease, diabetes, etc.)
Anyone interested in plant-based diets or disease prevention
core_themes: Preventing and reversing chronic illnesses through nutrition
The impact of plant-based diets on health
Empowering individuals to take control of their health
Critique of standard dietary guidelines and processed foods
primary_purpose: To educate readers on how certain foods and lifestyle choices, based on the latest scientific research, can prevent and sometimes reverse the leading causes of death—encouraging a plant-based, whole-food diet as a central method of improving health and longevity.

structure_format.narrative_style: Accessible and engaging, supported by scientific references and practical advice
structure_format.organization: Divided into two major sections: the first covers the top causes of premature death and how diet can impact them; the second provides practical guidelines—the ‘Daily Dozen’—for healthy eating habits.
features: Practical ‘take home’ messages at chapter ends
Detailed references and resources for further study

key_concepts_lessons: Many leading causes of death are preventable through dietary and lifestyle choices.
A diet rich in whole, plant-based foods can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and other chronic illnesses.
Animal products and highly processed foods are linked to increased health risks.
Scientific evidence should drive nutritional advice, not industry influence or tradition.
Implementing simple habits (like the ‘Daily Dozen’) can make healthy eating practical and sustainable.
style_tone: Accessible to lay readers, but detailed enough for professionals
notable_features: Heavy reliance on peer-reviewed scientific research
Debunks common health myths and misinformation
Focuses on empowerment and actionable information
cultural_historical_context: Released amidst rising awareness of the impact of chronic diseases and interest in plant-based diets, the book reflected shifting attitudes toward preventative health and skepticism toward traditional nutritional guidelines. It also contributed to the broader popularization of plant-based lifestyles in Western wellness culture.
reception_impact: Bestseller in health and wellness categories
Widely praised for making complex science accessible
Lauded by advocates of plant-based nutrition
Critically acclaimed for depth of research, though sometimes challenged by proponents of omnivorous diets
Ongoing influence through related resources (website, videos, companion cookbooks)
comparable_titles: Eat to Live by Joel Fuhrman
The China Study by T. Colin Campbell and Thomas M. Campbell
Whole: Rethinking the Science of Nutrition by T. Colin Campbell
Forks Over Knives: The Plant-Based Way to Health by Gene Stone
